objective: Improve reciprocal host-normalized min-of-N reference/target latency for a single-threaded DuckDB physical-filter microbenchmark over fixed SF1 input. Exact typed output, a frozen upstream physical-filter test subset, and whole-tree peak memory no greater than baseline plus 10% are hard gates. Only src/execution/operator/filter/physical_filter.cpp is mutable.

meta.provenance: duckdb/duckdb at exact revision 117e1a46be1c903c5a36ee3c881c125597f93c60, layered with trusted evaluator glue in synthetic baseline commit lineage; fixed SF1 database SHA-256 1e2a17dedac4da19efb6c8c154b82042cd78f1faa862a8a1b7d95f717ea0bb94; q is the host-normalized reference-yardstick score NORM_CONST(1.0)*min(reference)/min(target) over 7 timed fresh-process pairs (2 warmups), where the filter-free reference query is run by a SEPARATE pristine runner built+sealed from the trusted baseline with NO candidate overlay (candidate-independent), and every sample runs in a cgroup leaf capped to one core-equivalent (cpu.max) and one task (pids.max=1); trusted repeated-baseline fresh-container aggregates [1.0311366780691889,1.0186448748475132,1.0142276475913028] give qBase=1.0311366780691889, sample sigma=0.008769952071934352, qReference=qBase+max(5*sigma,0.05*abs(qBase-0))=1.0826935119691889; whole-tree cgroup memory.peak gate at baseline 115000 KiB +10%; terminal holdout seal with no optimizer pilots

measurement.platform: linux/arm64 Docker Desktop on Apple M3 Max; final recalibration required on frozen GCE Linux host
measurement.q: host-normalized reference-yardstick score NORM_CONST(1.0) * min(reference)/min(target) over 7 timed fresh-process target/reference pairs (2 warmups); the filter-free reference query never invokes the mutable PhysicalFilter and is run by a SEPARATE pristine runner built+sealed from the trusted baseline with no candidate overlay, so it is candidate-independent; each sample runs in its own cgroup leaf capped to one core (cpu.max) and one task (pids.max=1); the per-binary minimum cancels shared-host contention drift while rewarding a genuinely faster filter path

robustnessReview.protectedPathEscape: the broker protects the evaluator, build graph, runner, tests, dependencies, assets, and every source file outside the one-file physical-filter envelope; the evaluator independently rejects additions and every symlink
robustnessReview.benchmarkSpecialCasing: independently authored, non-tautological train and validation predicates (distinct selective length thresholds over lower()/upper() case kernels) exercise the same physical-filter kernel over the same fixed database and exact typed output; any pass-through of the input chunk changes the selected row set and fails the exact-output oracle, the frozen upstream test subset includes a length-case filter test whose predicates drop rows, and split-inverting diagnostics must lose on validation
robustnessReview.fixtureFingerprinting: assets are hash-verified, copied read-only, and unmounted before candidate build; every sample starts with a swept /tmp and /dev/shm, a fresh working directory, and fresh IPC and NET namespaces
robustnessReview.outputFabrication: each process stdout is checked against an oracle retained only in the trusted parent after the sealed asset mount is removed
robustnessReview.timerTampering: CLOCK_MONOTONIC timing surrounds each full process in the trusted Python parent and the score is the per-binary minimum of 7 timed reference/target pairs (min(reference)/min(target)); no candidate-linked clock or reported duration is accepted
robustnessReview.processLifecycle: every sample runs in its own root-owned cgroup leaf (cpu.max one core, pids.max=1) with a fresh process group and bounded timeout; the leaf is killed and retired via cgroup.kill after every leg, and a pre-sample sweep kills any surviving demoted process and reaps orphans adopted by the pid-1 evaluator (a non-empty cgroup.procs after a sample fails it)
robustnessReview.binaryMutation: the candidate runner and the pristine reference runner are each copied into a root-owned read-only sealed directory before any sample runs and the entire build tree is deleted; peak memory comes from the whole-tree cgroup memory.peak, never a candidate-writable file or a single-child rusage
robustnessReview.buildScriptMutation: CMake, compiler flags, evaluator, worker, runner, and tests are protected; every evaluation rebuilds submitted source from scratch
